implementation_notes: Modern C++ defaults to a standard-library associative container of type-erased callables: `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::function<Response(const Request&)>>` (or `std::map` when iteration order matters) filled once at startup, read with `find`/`contains` and invoked through `operator()`. What replaces the classic hand-written jump table is the container's own hash lookup plus `std::function`'s type erasure, so handlers may be free functions, lambdas or member functions bound with `std::mem_fn`; the table is enumerable for help texts and reachable from several modules through a registrar. This is the right default when keys are strings/ids, the key space is open or entries are added at runtime; when the alternatives are a closed set known at compile time, the `std::variant` + `std::visit` form is compiler-checked and avoids both the string keys and the per-call erasure.
pitfalls: `map[key]` default-constructs an empty `std::function` and the call then throws `std::bad_function_call` - use `find`/`at` and state the miss policy explicitly.

Every entry is type-erased: `std::function` may heap-allocate for larger captures and its calls cannot be inlined, so a table of lambdas loses to a dense `std::array` of plain function pointers inside a hot loop.
String keys are hashed and compared on each dispatch, and a typo in a literal silently registers a second entry instead of failing to compile - prefer enum or `constexpr` keys.
A file-scope table that calls into other translation units during initialisation is subject to static initialisation order: build it on first use or from `main`.

variants.name: std::variant + std::visit over the closed set of operations
variants.implementation_notes: For a closed set of operation types, `std::variant` is the table: `std::visit` indexes a compiler-generated table of function pointers keyed by the variant's `index()`, so dispatch is O(1), nothing is type-erased and a missing overload is a compile error. The overload-pattern helper (`template<class... Ts> struct overload : Ts... { using Ts::operator()...; }`) lets the handlers be plain lambdas, one per alternative. Choose this when the set of commands/messages is known at build time and exhaustiveness is worth more than runtime registration; choose the function map when keys arrive as data.
pitfalls: `std::visit` requires every alternative to be handled: adding a type to the variant breaks compilation until a handler exists - a feature, but a build-time coupling across all visitors.
Multi-variant visitation costs the product of the alternatives in table size and compile time, so it does not scale to many independent variants.
The variant form fixes the key set at compile time; a plugin or configuration-driven key space cannot be expressed this way and needs the function map or an `std::any`-keyed fallback.

variants.name: Array-of-labels jump table (GNU computed goto) for interpreter loops
variants.idiom_name: static const void* const table[] = {&&op_add, ...}; goto *table[opcode]
variants.implementation_notes: The fastest interpreter dispatch known: an array of label addresses (`&&label`) indexed by the opcode and a single `goto *table[op]` at the end of every handler, so each opcode gets its own branch-prediction site instead of one shared switch jump (CPython, Lua and Ruby YARV all ship this form behind a compiler check, with CPython reporting 15-20% over switch threading). It is a GNU/Clang extension, not standard C++, and it is the one variant where the table is literally a jump table; keep it for interpreter cores where dispatch dominates, and prefer the function map everywhere else.
pitfalls: The opcode indexes the table unchecked: an out-of-range value is an arbitrary jump (remote-code-execution class bug), so validate or generate the opcodes yourself.
Compilers may merge or cross-jump the indirect branches and destroy the prediction benefit; CPython has to pin flags such as -fno-gcse, so this variant must be measured, not assumed.
Labels-as-values is a compiler extension: it does not exist in MSVC or standard C++, so this variant needs a feature check and a switch-based fallback.
